# Build: enforce-the-merge-queue-every-finished-build-goe

## Brett said (verbatim)
At: 2026-11-10T16:43:57.553Z
> What happened to the merge queue? We need to start enforcing that. Everything needs to go into the merge queue so we can make one build out of it before we send it to CI.

## What to build
Continue build "Enforce the merge queue: every finished build goes into it and is batched into one combined build before CI" (enforce-the-merge-queue-every-finished-build-goe) — Phase 1, model Opus.
What Brett asked for (build-origin@1, his words come first; a paraphrase never replaces them):
Brett said (2026-11-10 16:43):
"What happened to the merge queue? We need to start enforcing that. Everything needs to go into the merge queue so we can make one build out of it before we send it to CI."
Model switches: a downgrade (e.g. Fable → Opus) is fine. Fable upgrades need no approval right now (Brett, Nov 4 2026: "If it needs Fable, set it to be Fable"): a step that needs Fable (schemas, asset types, contracts, engines/kernel, cross-app protocols) is set to Fable and runs on Fable; the switch is recorded on the build. Never launch a step on a higher model than it is pinned to: raise the step first.
Rules: stay in this one session; no sub-agents; steps ≤ 30 min; read only the files listed; stop at the end of this phase.
Look: UI code (handwritten or generated) conforms to the hot-swappable asset system: every colour, size, spacing, font, radius and border comes from asset tokens (--fx-* colour/style, --fx-type-* / --fx-dens-* / --fx-size-* scale, --fx-radius-*, --fx-border-w; Kotlin: Axf.colors / Axf.type / Axf.space / Axf.shapes), framework controls instead of raw ones, no var() fallbacks. `node framework/cli/check-theme.mjs` and `check-controls.mjs` must pass (CI fails otherwise); `node framework/cli/scale-adopt.mjs <path>` moves most literals onto the tokens.
API: Everything comes with an API (Brett, Nov 8 2026): anything this build adds or changes that has a UI gets full API control: a deep link that opens it (console_show / console_open target), its state readable, and every action and setting it offers callable without the UI, through the console API (REST), MCP tools (console actions, plugin commands, control@1 for tokens and planner items), the CLI and voice (AmberX), all four the same. A UI-only feature is not done; say in the PR how each one is reached.
Steps in this phase (3 left, ~1.3 h):
[ ] s1 (~30 min) Enforce for all builds, no exceptions: when a build finishes it goes into the merge queue (never straight to main or its own CI run). The merge queue combines the queued builds into one batch build, resolves conflicts, then sends that single build to CI; on green it lands and redeploys. Reconcile with auto-land-every-build and the Batch Manager build. No AI for the queue logic. Full API control.
[ ] s2 (~30 min) What happened to the merge queue? We need to start enforcing that. Everything needs to go into the merge queue so we can make one build out of it before we send it to CI.
[ ] s3 (~20 min) Tests green, report _claude/builds/reports/enforce-the-merge-queue-every-finished-build-goe.md, THREADS row, commit, push, PR
Read first: _claude/builds/reports/enforce-the-merge-queue-every-finished-build-goe.md, _claude/THREADS.md
Tick each step: node apps/console-web/plugins/build-orchestrator/orchestrator.mjs act step enforce-the-merge-queue-every-finished-build-goe <stepId> done — it reaches main at once (builds-live). Link your branch / PR: node framework/cli/builds-live.mjs link enforce-the-merge-queue-every-finished-build-goe --branch <b> --pr <n>.
Watch live: when you start on a screen, run `node framework/cli/axf.mjs focus <app> [route] [css-selector] --note "…"` so the live preview follows you.
Screenshots that are not for approval (checking a screen, live captures, before/after): axf shot <file> --name "…" --app … --screen … --group "<build name>" (UI Review → Screenshots; ui-review-item@1), never the review queue.

## Pipeline
This session was started by the orchestrator's dispatcher on Claude account mossesx-max- for the Opus phase. Tick every step as you finish it (orchestrator.mjs act step enforce-the-merge-queue-every-finished-build-goe <stepId> done). When this phase's steps are done, stop: the dispatcher starts the next phase on the right account. If you must stop early with steps left, say why in a build note (orchestrator.mjs act note enforce-the-merge-queue-every-finished-build-goe "…"); the build goes back to Pending for Brett.

open: UI Review shots aren't taken yet: this session had no way to render the console. Needed: Settings → Plugins → Push banner (Batch switch + PRs in one batch), and the merge queue view with a batch line. Desktop and phone.

`menu-reach.mts` now sees nav entries in multi-line blocks and imported constants. `agent-voice` and `codebase-changes` reach their pages only through an `.open` action, not a `nav:` menu item. The "nav entry in the app menu" rule still uses the old one-line parse so this doesn't turn CI red; those two are left for their own builds.
Another check that only fails locally: `test_wall_users.py` "the page itself" needs a built web bundle.
Bisection costs about log2(batch size) extra runs for each broken PR in a batch. With the default of 8, that's at most 3 extra runs.
`.axf-focus.json` (gitignored, written by the live-preview focus tool) makes `plugin-lifecycle check push-banner` flag a stale reference in local worktrees only. CI never sees it.
`check-headless-tabs.mts` fails inside a Claude session's environment (it reads the session's own memory chain) and passes in a clean one (63/63). This is not a main issue.
